issues.title: Handler logic mixed in schema file
issues.description: The rule requires that schema and handler logic are separated into different files. However, the schema file `booking.output.ts` now contains a handler method `cleanEmailForDisplay()` that performs email validation and transformation logic, mixing schema definition with handler logic in the same file.
issues.rule_name: Schema and Handler Files Must Be Separated with Type-Safe Patterns

issues.title: Lost `this` context in displayGuests mapping causes runtime error
issues.description: In the `getOutputBooking` method at line 171, the code passes `this.getDisplayEmail` directly to the `map` function without binding the `this` context. This causes a runtime error because when `getDisplayEmail` is invoked inside the `map` callback, `this` will be `undefined`, resulting in "Cannot read property 'replace' of undefined" or similar errors. The arrow function `(guest: string) => this.getDisplayEmail(guest)` was removed, which was necessary to preserve the `this` binding. This will break all bookings that have guests.

issues.title: Recurring seated bookings returned in wrong order
issues.description: In the `getOutputRecurringSeatedBookings` method at line 424, the sort operation that orders bookings chronologically by start time has been removed. The original code sorted bookings with `.sort((a, b) => new Date(a.start).getTime() - new Date(b.start).getTime())` to ensure they are returned in chronological order. Without this sorting, recurring bookings will be returned in an arbitrary order (based on how they were stored in the database or map), which breaks the expected API contract and will confuse clients expecting chronological ordering of recurring events.

issues.title: Unnecessary regex processing on literal "unknown" string
issues.description: In the `getHost` method at line 219, when the user is null/unknown, the code now calls `this.getDisplayEmail("unknown")` instead of directly setting `displayEmail: "unknown"`. This causes unnecessary regex processing on the literal string "unknown" which has no CUID suffix to remove. While this doesn't break functionality, it adds unnecessary computational overhead and is semantically incorrect - the getDisplayEmail method is designed to strip CUID suffixes from actual email addresses, not process placeholder strings. This represents a performance issue and code smell that violates the principle of only processing data when necessary.

issues.title: Service file uses disallowed '.service.ts' suffix / naming convention violation
issues.description: Rule 1 disallows dot-suffix service filenames like '.service.ts' and requires service files to be named '<Entity>Service.ts' with matching PascalCase. This PR modifies a service located at 'services/output.service.ts', which violates the naming convention.
issues.rule_name: Rule 1: Repository and Service Classes Must Follow Naming Conventions

issues.title: Line(s) exceed the 110 character line width requirement
issues.description: The added assignment line is longer than the 110 character limit required by the Biome formatting rules for TS/JS files.
issues.rule_name: Rule 3: Use Biome for Code Formatting with Standardized Configuration

issues.description: The PR introduces improperly indented JSON (the 'required' key is moved to column 1). This indicates the JSON was not kept formatted per the repository’s formatting/lint-staged expectations (Biome format for JSON).

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #25593 - fix(api): return original email without OAuth suffix in bookings

structured_output.summary:
The PR adds a `displayEmail` field next to the existing `email` on booking API v2 (2024-08-13) responses. `displayEmail` is the address with the `+{cuid}` OAuth-client suffix stripped, and `email` is left unchanged for backwards compatibility. The change is applied to hosts, attendees, seated and recurring-seated attendees, `bookingFieldsResponses` (`displayEmail` and `displayGuests`), and `reassignedTo`. It touches `OutputBookingsService_2024_08_13`, the response DTOs in `packages/platform/types`, the OpenAPI JSON, and many e2e specs.

The core approach is sound: keeping the original field and adding a new one avoids a breaking change for platform customers, and the new managed-user e2e tests check the suffixed and stripped values. However, the diff contains an unrelated behavior regression. It removes the `sort` by start time from `getOutputRecurringSeatedBookings`, which changes the response order of recurring seated bookings and is not mentioned in the PR. There are also smaller issues: an unanchored regex that can mangle legitimate plus-tags, dead code in the DTO, and malformed OpenAPI JSON indentation.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The removed sort in getOutputRecurringSeatedBookings is an unintended regression. The base version sorted the result by start time, and the caller in bookings.service.ts (GET by uid for recurring seated bookings) now returns whatever order the repository gives. That needs to be restored or justified before merge. The remaining items are medium and low: a regex that is too broad and has no edge-case tests, plus cleanup in the DTO, the service, and the OpenAPI file.

architecture.overview:
Booking responses in API v2 (2024-08-13) are built by `OutputBookingsService_2024_08_13` in `apps/api/v2/src/ee/bookings/2024-08-13/services/output.service.ts`. Each `getOutput*` method maps Prisma booking rows into plain objects, then runs `plainToClass` with `excludeAll` against output DTOs in `packages/platform/types/bookings/2024-08-13/outputs/booking.output.ts`. Those DTOs control which fields are exposed. `bookings.service.ts` calls the output service from the controllers, and the public OpenAPI document in `docs/api-reference/v2/openapi.json` is generated from the DTOs.

This PR leaves the existing `email` fields alone and adds a sibling `displayEmail` on each attendee, host, reassignedTo, and bookingFieldsResponses object. A private `getDisplayEmail` helper strips the `+{cuid}` suffix with `/\+[a-zA-Z0-9]{25}/`. Guest arrays get a matching `displayGuests` array. The PR also has one unrelated change: `getOutputRecurringSeatedBookings` no longer sorts its results by start time.
steps: Entry point: the bookings controllers call `BookingsService` in `bookings.service.ts`. For a recurring seated booking, `getBookingByUid` gathers the rows and calls `getOutputRecurringSeatedBookings` (around line 611).

Mapping layer: `OutputBookingsService_2024_08_13` builds plain booking objects. The PR adds `getDisplayEmail` (output.service.ts lines 96-98) and calls it for each attendee, for the host returned by `getHost`, and for the `reassignedTo` payload.

Bookings-responses post-processing: `getOutputBooking` and `getOutputRecurringBooking` set `bookingFieldsResponses.displayEmail` and `displayGuests` after `plainToClass`, since `bookingFieldsResponses` is attached manually.
DTO contract: `booking.output.ts` declares `displayEmail` on `BookingAttendee`, `BookingHost`, and `ReassignedToDto`. Those DTOs drive the OpenAPI JSON, which is updated by hand in this PR.
Ordering side effect: `getOutputRecurringSeatedBookings` used to sort by start time and now returns the repository order. This is the one behavior change outside the stated scope.

findings.title: Removed start-time sort from recurring seated bookings output
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/api/v2/src/ee/bookings/2024-08-13/services/output.service.ts`, `getOutputRecurringSeatedBookings` (around lines 411-425) was changed to `return transformed;`, which removed the sort by start time that existed in the base commit. Restore the sort, so the method returns `transformed.sort((a, b) => new Date(a.start).getTime() - new Date(b.start).getTime())`, matching the other recurring output methods in the same file. Keep the displayEmail changes intact. If there is a deliberate reason to drop the sort, document it in a comment instead. Check that the recurring seated e2e tests in `apps/api/v2/src/ee/bookings/2024-08-13/controllers/e2e/seated-bookings.e2e-spec.ts` still pass.

findings.title: Unanchored regex strips legitimate plus-tags
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/api/v2/src/ee/bookings/2024-08-13/services/output.service.ts`, the private `getDisplayEmail` helper (around lines 96-98) uses `/\+[a-zA-Z0-9]{25}/`, which is not anchored to the local part before `@`. It can strip a user-chosen plus-tag of 25 or more characters and leaves the rest of the address corrupted. Change the pattern so it only matches the CUID suffix directly before the `@` in the local part, for example with a lookahead for `@`. Then add a focused unit test file next to the service that covers an address with no suffix, a standard CUID suffix, and a 25+ alphanumeric user tag that must be preserved. Keep the same helper name so existing callers still work.

findings.title: Unbound method reference passed to map
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/api/v2/src/ee/bookings/2024-08-13/services/output.service.ts`, `getOutputBooking` (around lines 167-174) calls `.map(this.getDisplayEmail)` without binding `this`. It works only because the helper does not use `this`. Change it to an arrow function, `.map((guest: string) => this.getDisplayEmail(guest))`, to match the form used in `getOutputRecurringBooking` in the same file.

findings.title: Unused static helper duplicates the service's email cleaner
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/platform/types/bookings/2024-08-13/outputs/booking.output.ts`, the `BookingAttendee` class has a static `cleanEmailForDisplay` method (around lines 59-62) that nothing calls and that duplicates the regex in `getDisplayEmail` in `apps/api/v2/src/ee/bookings/2024-08-13/services/output.service.ts`. Remove the static method and its misleading comment. If a shared helper is needed, export a single regex or function from one place and use it in both files.

findings.title: Malformed indentation in edited OpenAPI JSON
findings.fixPrompt: In `docs/api-reference/v2/openapi.json`, the `"required": [` keys added in this PR (around lines 31729, 31833, 32267, and 33370) start at column 0. Re-indent them to match the surrounding object keys, or, better, regenerate the OpenAPI file from the updated DTOs in `packages/platform/types/bookings/2024-08-13/outputs/booking.output.ts` so the checked-in file matches the generator output.

findings.title: Duplicated displayEmail/displayGuests post-processing across booking outputs
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/api/v2/src/ee/bookings/2024-08-13/services/output.service.ts`, the `displayEmail` and `displayGuests` post-processing is duplicated in `getOutputBooking` (around lines 158-174) and `getOutputRecurringBooking`. Extract it into one private helper, such as `addDisplayFields(bookingTransformed)`, that sets `bookingFieldsResponses.displayEmail` and `displayGuests`, and call it from both methods. Keep behavior unchanged.

findings.title: Targeted e2e coverage for the new display fields
findings.body: The new `describe("displayEmail fields")` block in `managed-user-bookings.e2e-spec.ts` covers the important cases from the PR description. It checks that `hosts[0].email` keeps the suffix and `hosts[0].displayEmail` drops it, that an attendee managed user gets the same split and that `bookingFieldsResponses` carries both values, and that `guests` keeps the suffix while `displayGuests` drops it. Using the real managed-user fixtures makes these assertions meaningful, not just `toBeDefined`. Existing `toEqual` expectations across the other e2e specs were updated to include `displayEmail`, so any accidental omission of the field would fail there too.

findings.title: Backward-compatible additive API change
findings.body: The PR keeps `email` exactly as before and only adds `displayEmail`, `displayGuests`, and the related fields. That is the right design for an API version that is already published to platform customers. Clients that parse `email` see no change, and clients that want clean addresses have a new field to use. The OpenAPI changes are additive, so the oasdiff breaking-change check should only flag additions.
